stories.standfirst: Gold has a way of ending arguments, and {winner} has been first to reach it, claiming the Golden Showdown for {winnerClub}.
paragraphs: Let the presses run slowly tonight, because this edition is printed in gold. {winner} was the first manager to reach the summit of the Golden Showdown, and no second chance exists for {loser} to answer. The race has ended.

Nothing in the rules asks for a combined tally or a shared reckoning. One manager had to arrive first, and {winner} arrived with {winnerPoints} to the {loserPoints} of {loser}. That order of arrival is the whole story.
Historians will open this page for generations. They will find {winnerClub} at the head of the roll, and they will find that the order of arrival never needed a second reading.

pullquote.text: Gold goes to whoever arrives first, and the Gazette has watched the arrival.

stories.standfirst: The history books have a new first line, and it reads {winner}, who stood alone at the top of the Golden Showdown.
paragraphs: Somewhere in the Gazette archive a page has been cleared for a name that was not there yesterday. {winner} has won the Golden Showdown, becoming the first manager to reach the line that no ordinary Showdown ever draws.

It is a rare thing for a rivalry to be remembered by its ending. Across {seasonsTotal} seasons, {winnerClub} and {loserClub} wrote the longest chapter this newspaper has known, and the final paragraph belongs to {winner}.
Future editions will refer to this one in a lowered voice. Some pages are simply bigger than the rest, and the archivist has already reached for the good paper.

pullquote.text: Every archive has one page that the others are arranged around.

stories.standfirst: A dynasty is a habit that refuses to stop, and {winnerClub} under {winner} has made one worth the crown of gold.
paragraphs: Few clubs are ever called a dynasty while the ink is still wet. Yet {winner} has carried {winnerClub} through {seasonsTotal} seasons of relentless accumulation and has become the first to complete the Golden Showdown, with {loser} chasing to the very end.

The measure of a dynasty is not a single glorious night. It is the quiet repetition of excellence, season after season, until the rest of the contest can only watch. {winnerPoints} points is what that repetition looks like when written down.
{loserClub} was the rival every dynasty needs, and the pursuit was real. The record now belongs to {winner}, and the word will not fade from the clubhouse wall.

pullquote.text: A dynasty is only visible once it has stopped being surprised by itself.

stories.standfirst: In a Showdown measured one manager at a time, {winner} has been the first to cross the golden line.
paragraphs: This is the edition that every other edition was practice for. The Golden Showdown asks one question of each manager, and {winner} answered it before {loser} could, finishing on {winnerPoints} when {loserPoints} was the best the pursuit could manage.
There is no consolation in a race like this, only a clear order of finish. The gap of {margin} is the distance between first and second, and in a contest this long even that gap is a long way earned.
Gold is cold to the touch and warm to the memory. The Gazette prints it with pride, and the shelf at {winnerClub} has a new centrepiece.

pullquote.text: We printed a great many headlines to reach this one.

stories.standfirst: Keep this one, fold it carefully and tell your grandchildren: {winner} has won the Golden Showdown.
paragraphs: Newsprint rarely deserves to be kept, but this page does. {winner} won the Golden Showdown by being first to the line, and the whole of {seasonsTotal} seasons has led to this front page and this single name.

Collectors will argue about margins and moments. The Gazette prefers the plain fact that {winnerClub} got there ahead of {loserClub}, and that nobody can take the order of arrival away from {winner} now.
Frame it, pin it or tuck it inside a favourite book. In years to come it will still read exactly as grandly as it does tonight.

pullquote.text: Some front pages are made to be thrown away and this was not one.

stories.standfirst: The long road is over and the gold is awarded, with {winner} first home after a Showdown that asked for everything.
paragraphs: Nobody wins a Golden Showdown by accident. It takes patience, appetite and the nerve to keep collecting while a rival keeps pace, and {winner} had all three as {winnerClub} became the first to complete the climb.

{loser} deserves a page of its own in this story, because a chase is only as good as the pace it sets. {loserClub} set a hard one, and that is why the winning total of {winnerPoints} carries such weight.
The rivalry will go on in conversation, as the best rivalries do. For now the title is settled, and it is gold.

pullquote.text: The chase made the gold shine, and the winner made it gleam.

stories.standfirst: Somewhere in a quiet room, a cabinet is being rearranged, because {winnerClub} has won the Golden Showdown.
paragraphs: The most dramatic moments in football often happen in silence. {winner} has completed the Golden Showdown, and the first thing {winnerClub} will need is shelf space, because gold of this scale does not sit politely among the rest.
{seasonsTotal} seasons of work have been compressed into a single line of print. It reads {winner} first and {loser} second, and the line is as short as the work behind it was long.
Trophy cabinets are the quiet storytellers of the game. This one now holds the loudest object it has ever been given.

pullquote.text: Make room in the cabinet, because the gold does not fit politely.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: It ends as legends end, with a name, a number it will not repeat here and a rival who made it hard.
paragraphs: There comes a moment in every great rivalry when the story outgrows the newspaper. {winner} has won the Golden Showdown, and the Gazette, which has printed everything else, hesitates over what to add to that sentence.
Perhaps nothing at all is needed. {winnerClub} finished ahead, {loserClub} pushed it all the way, and across {seasonsTotal} seasons two managers produced a contest worth the gold that closes it.
Close the ledger gently and leave the lights on for a while. A page like this deserves a slow and thankful reading.

pullquote.text: There are headlines you write, and there are headlines that arrive.
